independence: No other worker outputs read; independently derived then sent results to parent.
scoped_result: Exact positive mass-load reduction, sharp insufficiency countermodels and boundary envelopes, goal-adjoint certificate, exact-mean plus finite-deadline coupling contract for dangling components.
decisive_findings: Exact two-terminal Schur response plus total hidden mass does not determine directional mean; fixed response family changes mass allocation continuously.
A weak two-boundary pair has exactly identical C, Z and deletion conductance 1e-12, yet directional mean ratio is exactly 5e11.
Mass-preserving Schur reduction already exists in graph transformation; unmodified pinned PyGT recovered all five adversarial means to <=2.22e-16 relative float error.
One-boundary components transfer all their mass without internal-rate values for exact means, given verified topology and reversible mass/conductance assumptions.
Boundary-only mass envelopes have width sum_D W_D osc_BD(h), universally sharp for two boundaries even with a fixed exact component response.
Mean-preserving 2-state model overestimates one 3-state deadline survival by about 1e12.

A dangling-component trace/race coupling returns exact means separately from a deadline envelope without internal excursion distributions; at T=20 the scalar fixture has a rational outward certificate with ratio <1.000486, while T=100 fails relative accuracy.
A star with k distinct leaf rates has exact first-passage rational degree k+1, so no fixed-state exact deadline representation is guaranteed.
Heavy-leaf orientation oracle needs Omega(n) worst-case access even when exact capacity and total mass are supplied for free.

comparator.name: Unmodified PyGT.GT
comparator.performance_claim: NONE; only small correctness fixtures executed.

costs.explicit_input_access: Omega(total encoded input length); topology/component processing O(n+m).
costs.general_positive_elimination: O(sum d_k^2) arithmetic, worst-case O(n^3), O(n^2) fill storage; mass load shares the elimination.
costs.one_boundary_aggregate: Internal rates unnecessary for means only when topology and total mass are supplied/verified; equally credited to all methods.
costs.mass_envelope: Graph pass after boundary potentials, masses and boundaries are acquired; boundary solve costs remain.
costs.adjoint_certificate: Requires residual/flow data and usually additional solve work; weak heavy mass can cancel energy-smallness gains.
costs.deadline: Dynamic memory/frequency work or additional states generally remains; coupling envelope useful only when entry risk is small relative to requested survival.
costs.precision: Positive forest formula gives data-perturbation bound independent of rate dynamic range; directed arithmetic and exponent representation remain separate obligations.

limitations: No novelty/priority claim for Schur, graph transformation, mass-load elimination, forest formulas or coupling.
No full molecular network, LJ38 run, physical parameter uncertainty enclosure, unseen-channel bound, energy/memory measurement or end-to-end scientific speed comparison.
PyGT float output was checked against exact small oracles but not itself outward-rounded.
The general-core matrix exponential version of the deadline coupling theorem was proved but not benchmarked.
